| `CYLTabBarMinimizeBehavior` | How the tab bar reacts to scrolling (issue #13). One value for every style, set with `-[CYLTabBarController cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior]`: - Liquid Glass (iOS 26+): passed to the native `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior`; the system minimizes (shrinks) the tab bar, and the plus button is centered on its tab meanwhile. - FlatDesign: the tab bar is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the current page scrolls. - Classic tab bar (iOS 25 and earlier, and iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar, with its plus button, is hidden and shown with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` while the current page scrolls. The values match `UITabBarMinimizeBehavior` one to one. | TODO |

| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar 0` | The `UITabBarAppearance` of the flat design tab bar, like `-[UITabBar standardAppearance]`: one appearance object styles the system tab bar (Liquid Glass and the classic style) and this tab bar alike. Nil (the default) keeps the flat design look and the properties below. `CYLTabBarController` assigns `tabBarController.tabBar.standardAppearance` here when the app has set one, so setting the system tab bar's appearance is enough; assigning this property directly also works. When the selected item has its own `-[CYLFlatDesignTabBarItem standardAppearance]`, the whole bar uses that one while it is selected, as `UITabBar` does. Mapping (UITabBarAppearance → flat design tab bar): backgroundEffect → the background blur (nil: no blur) backgroundColor → the background color backgroundImage → the background image backgroundImageContentMode → the background image's content mode shadowImage → the top shadow line (its own height; tinted by shadowColor if template) shadowColor → a hairline at the top when there is no shadowImage (nil/clear: none) selectionIndicatorImage → drawn behind the selected item selectionIndicatorTintColor → tints the selection indicator image stackedItemPositioning → .centered lays the items out centered; .fill / .automatic fill the width stackedItemWidth → the item width when centered (0: equal share of the width) stackedItemSpacing → the spacing between items when centered stackedLayoutAppearance.normal / .selected / .disabled (UITabBarItemStateAppearance): titleTextAttributes → title font, color and other attributes (they override the item's own) titlePositionAdjustment → the title offset when the item has none (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment` wins, as on the system tab bar) iconColor → the icon tint color (template images) badgeBackgroundColor → the badge background color badgeTextAttributes → the badge font and text color badgePositionAdjustment → the badge center offset Not mapped: inline/compact inline layouts (the flat design bar is always stacked), scroll edge appearances, `badgeTitlePositionAdjustment` and the focused state. Badge values a state does not customize (equal to a new `UITabBarAppearance`) leave the badge's own settings and `CYLBadgeAppearance` in place. | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar tintColor` | — | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar barTintColor` | default is nil | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar backgroundImage` | The background image will be tiled to fit, even if it was not created via the UIImage resizableImage methods. | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar shadowImage` | Default is nil. When non-nil, a custom shadow image to show instead of the default shadow image. For a custom shadow to be shown, a custom background image must also be set with -setBackgroundImage: (if the default background image is used, the default shadow image will be used). | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar useLayoutSafeAreaInsets` | Whether the buttons stay clear of the left/right safe area (e.g. a landscape notch). The background always spans the full width. The one-sided inset of a vertical status bar (the folded iPhone Duo's right-hand status column) is controlled separately by `respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea` (ignored by default). | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea` | Default is NO. Whether the buttons also stay clear of the inset that a vertical status bar adds on one side, e.g. the 84 pt column on the right of the folded iPhone Duo held upright (iOS 27.1 SDK), where the status bar (Wi-Fi, battery) moves to the trailing edge. NO: that one-sided inset is ignored, so the buttons span the full width and stay centered on screen; the last button can sit partly under the status column. YES: the buttons stay inside the safe area, so the row is shifted left by that column. A vertical status bar is told apart by its inset being on one side only; a landscape notch insets both sides and is still handled by `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets`. Has no effect when `useLayoutSafeAreaInsets` is NO. Only matters while the vertical bar is shown. This property does not switch the vertical bar on or off; that is `CYLTabBarController.allowsVerticalBar` (or a screen's own `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`). With the vertical bar off the status bar is horizontal, there is no one-sided inset, and both values give the same layout. | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar context` | This can be left unset; the default is CYLTabBarController. If set, please implement the `+[CYLPlusButton tabBarContext]` method in CYLPlusButton and ensure consistency. If neither is implemented, the default is CYLTabBarController for both. | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar -hasPlusButton` | — | TODO |
| `CYLFlatDesignTabBar -hasPlusChildViewController` | — | TODO |

### `CYLTabBarController.h`

| iOS 公开 API / iOS public API | 接口注释 / Comment | 鸿蒙对应接口 / HarmonyOS API |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `CYLViewDidLayoutSubViewsBlock` | Sets the block invoked in `-viewDidLayoutSubviews`. | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemTitle` | Optional per-tab colors (UIColor), in `tabBarItemsAttributes` (or `-updateTabBarItemAtIndex:attributes:`). See docs/Tab-Item-Colors.md. - `CYLTabBarItemTitleColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitleColor`: the title color, unselected / selected. - `CYLTabBarItemIconColor` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedIconColor`: the icon tint, unselected / selected. Only template images are tinted (`UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysTemplate`, SF Symbols); image names are drawn as original. - `CYLTabBarItemSelectedBackgroundColor`: fills the selected tab (classic tab bar and FlatDesign; Liquid Glass draws its own selection). Title and icon colors need iOS 13+ (`UITabBarAppearance`) and are ignored on iOS 12. Classic and Liquid Glass: the colors are written into the tab's own `UITabBarItem.standardAppearance` (and `scrollEdgeAppearance` on iOS 15+), a copy of the tab bar's appearance that is rebuilt when that one changes, as for `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`; an appearance you installed on the item is kept as the base. FlatDesign: the flat item's title attributes and `selectedBackgroundColor`. | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemSelectedTitle` | Optional title (NSString) shown while the tab is selected, like JD's "Home" tab that reads "Refresh" when it is selected; the tab shows `CYLTabBarItemTitle` again when another tab is selected. Works in every style (classic, Liquid Glass, FlatDesign). Pair it with `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` (or a Lottie animation, which replays on a re-tap) and with the reselect gesture (`cyl_tabBarItemGestureHandler`) to refresh on a second tap. It can be changed in place, like `CYLTabBarItemTitle`, with `-updateTabBarItemAtIndex:attributes:`. See docs/TabBarItem-Selected-Title.md. | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemImage` | `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` (and the dark keys below) take an image name or a UIImage. A name is the prepared form, recommended for most cases: it is rendered as original (the icon keeps its colors) and its dark image is loaded for you. A UIImage is used as it is: an image from `imageNamed:` has the `Automatic` rendering mode, which a tab bar tints as a template, so icons turn into one-color silhouettes unless you call `imageWithRenderingMode:UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysOriginal` first. | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` | — | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemDarkImage` | Optional dark images for `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage`, as a name or a UIImage. The tab then shows them where the interface style is dark (system setting or `overrideUserInterfaceStyle`) and switches by itself. Not needed when the image has a Dark appearance in the asset catalog or a "<name>_dark" image exists (`UIImage.cyl_darkImageNameSuffix`); when given, they replace those. | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemSelectedDarkImage` | — | TODO |
| `CYLTabBarItemImageURL` | Optional icons from the network, an NSURL or a URL string: unselected (`CYLTabBarItemImageURL`) and selected (`CYLTabBarItemSelectedImageURL`; without it the unselected one is used). `CYLTabBarItemImage` / `CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage` stay the default icons and the placeholders: the tab shows them until the download ends, and keeps them when it fails. The downloaded images then replace them, in every style, also over a Lottie icon, through `-setTabBarItemIcon:selectedIcon:size:atIndex:`, drawn with their own colors, a GIF animating. Any source that method takes works too (a file path, a UIImage...). `CYLTabBarItemImageURLSize` (an NSValue of CGSize) sets their size, the placeholder's by default. They are cached in memory and in the sandbox, see `CYLImageCache` to set how long and how much. @{ CYLTabBarItemTitle : @"Home", CYLTabBarItemImage : @"home_normal", // default and placeholder CYLTabBarItemSelectedImage : @"home_selected", CYLTabBarItemImageURL : @"https://example.com/home.png", // replaces them once downloaded CYLTabBarItemSelectedImageURL : @"https://example.com/home_selected.png" } | TODO |

A Lottie animation draws its own colors, so a tab with `CYLTabBarLottieURL` used to stay light in Dark Mode, whatever its images. With one of these, the tab shows the dark animation where the interface style is dark (system setting or `overrideUserInterfaceStyle`), and switches by itself, keeping the selected tab's state. CYLTabBarLottieURL : [NSURL fileURLWithPath:[[NSBundle mainBundle] pathForResource:@"tab_home" ofType:@"json"]], CYLTabBarLottieDarkURL : [NSURL fileURLWithPath:[[NSBundle mainBundle] pathForResource:@"tab_home_dark" ofType:@"json"]], | TODO |

| `CYLTabBarLottieDarkColors` | One Lottie file for both styles: an NSDictionary of keypath -> UIColor, the colors used where the interface style is dark. They are set with Lottie's official value providers (`setValueProvider(_:keypath:)` with a `ColorValueProvider`), which both rendering engines support, and removed in light mode, so the animation shows its own colors again. Switching keeps the view and its progress. Keypaths use Lottie's syntax: layer, group and item names joined by ".", with "*" for one name and "**" for any number (see `logHierarchyKeypaths()`): CYLTabBarLottieDarkColors : @{ @"Icon_Shop_Normal.**.Color" : [UIColor colorWithWhite:0.78 alpha:1], // gray strokes, lighter @"Icon_Shop_Active_Main.**.Color" : [UIColor colorWithRed:0.15 green:0.39 blue:0.16 alpha:1], }, Lottie 2.x (`CYLTabBarController/LottieObjectiveC`) ignores it; use `CYLTabBarLottieDarkFilePath` there. A dark file and dark colors can be combined: the colors then apply to the dark file. | TODO |

They work like the Lottie keys, and each library's own keys (`CYLTabBarLottie…`, `CYLTabBarPAG…`) keep working too. - `CYLTabBarAnimationURL` (NSURL) / `CYLTabBarAnimationFilePath` (NSString): the file; the URL wins. - `CYLTabBarAnimationSize`: the view size, an NSValue of CGSize (default: the icon placeholder size). - `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkURL` / `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkFilePath`: the Dark Mode version (#442). - `CYLTabBarAnimationDarkColors`: keypath -> UIColor for Dark Mode, for libraries that support it (Lottie 4.x). | TODO |

Without it, each tab's page comes from its page ID, see `CYLTabBarItemPageIdentifier`. - `CYLTabBarControllerTabBarItemsAttributes`: NSArray<NSDictionary *>, the item attributes (`CYLTabBarItemTitle`...). - `CYLTabBarControllerImageInsets`: NSValue of UIEdgeInsets, or "{top, left, bottom, right}", [t, l, b, r] or {top: , left: , bottom: , right: }. Default UIEdgeInsetsZero. - `CYLTabBarControllerTitlePositionAdjustment`: NSValue of UIOffset, or "{horizontal, vertical}", [h, v] or {horizontal: , vertical: }. Default UIOffsetZero. - `CYLTabBarControllerStyleType`: NSNumber of CYLTabBarStyleType, or "default", "system", "flatDesign", "liquidGlass". Default CYLTabBarStyleTypeDefault. - `CYLTabBarControllerContext`: NSString, see `context`. Default nil. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry`: CYLTabBarPageRegistry or any `CYLTabBarPageProviding` (code only), the page providers of this tab bar controller only, looked up before the shared registry. Lets several tab bars map one page ID to different pages. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageResolver`: CYLTabBarPageProvider block (code only), called for each tab whose page ID is not in `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry`, before the shared registry; return nil to go on looking. - `CYLTabBarControllerPageLookupOrder`: NSArray<CYLTabBarPageSource> (or a comma-separated string) of "instance", "resolver", "shared", "automatic": where pages are looked up, in order. Default all four, in that order. - `CYLTabBarControllerAutomaticPageRegistration`: NSNumber (BOOL), or "true" / "false"; NO leaves the classes that adopt `CYLTabBarPage` out of the lookup. Default YES. | TODO |

A value of the app is never replaced: tabs with a title, an item with its own `imageInsets` or `titlePositionAdjustment` (set on the item or with `CYLTabBarItemImageInsets` / `CYLTabBarItemTitlePositionAdjustment`), and a non-zero controller-level `imageInsets` / `titlePositionAdjustment` are left as they are. | `CYLTabBarController allowsVerticalBar` | Whether the system may show the bars in the vertical bar: a column on the leading or trailing edge that iOS 27.1 uses on some devices, such as the folded iPhone Duo. Defaults to NO. - NO: CYLTabBarController returns `UIVerticalBarBehaviorDisabled` from `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`, so the tab bar stays at the bottom and the status bar stays horizontal. Exception (issue #672): a screen that overrides `preferredVerticalBarBehavior` itself (the selected view controller, or the top view controller of a selected navigation controller) still decides for itself, e.g. return `UIVerticalBarBehaviorAutomatic` to opt in. - YES: the system default behaviour, as in 1.99.65 and earlier. `UITabBarController` passes the choice to the selected view controller, so each screen can still opt out by overriding `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`. This is a convenience switch for UIKit's `preferredVerticalBarBehavior`; a subclass may override that property directly instead. Changes apply immediately: the setter calls `setNeedsUpdateOfVerticalBarConfiguration`. Not related to `tabBarController.sidebar.preferredPlacement` / `sidebar.isAvailable` (iOS 27): those choose between the tab bar and an iPad-style sidebar when there is room for one (regular width) and need the `UITab` API; the vertical bar is used in compact width, where the sidebar is not available. Status with YES: Liquid Glass style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator (layout, Lottie icons, badges, plus button, re-tap, long press and drag). FlatDesign style verified on the iPhone Duo simulator: the status bar moves to the trailing column and the FlatDesign bar stays at the bottom with its items centered across the full width (see `CYLFlatDesignTabBar.respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea`). Folded iPhone Duo, FlatDesign, vertical status bar with centered items: tabBarController.allowsVerticalBar = YES; // respectsVerticalStatusBarSafeArea keeps its default NO No effect below iOS 27.1 or when built with an SDK older than iOS 27.1. | TODO |

| `CYLTabBarController(CYLTabBarMinimize) cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior` | How the tab bar reacts when the current page scrolls. Default `CYLTabBarMinimizeBehaviorAutomatic`. - Liquid Glass on iOS 26+ (every style except FlatDesign): sets the native `UITabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior`. The system shrinks the tab bar and picks the scroll view; choose it with `-[UIViewController setContentScrollView:forEdge:]` when a page has several. - FlatDesign: hides the tab bar with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page (the top page of a navigation controller) scrolls, and shows it again on the opposite scroll, when the page scrolls back to the top (OnScrollDown), and when another tab or page appears. A tab bar hidden by your own `-setTabBarHidden:` is left hidden. The scroll view is the page's `-contentScrollViewForEdge:NSDirectionalRectEdgeBottom`, otherwise the first scroll view in its view hierarchy. - Classic tab bar (every style except FlatDesign on iOS 25 and earlier, and on iOS 26 in UI compatibility mode): the system tab bar, with its plus button, is hidden with `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` when the selected page scrolls, and shown on the opposite scroll, at the top (OnScrollDown) and when another tab or page appears (animated by UIKit on iOS 18 and later, as FlatDesign before iOS 18). Pages pushed with `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed` are left to UIKit, and a tab bar at the top (not at the bottom) is never hidden. FlatDesign and the classic tab bar hide through the same public `-setTabBarHidden:animated:` you can call yourself; a tab bar you hid with it stays hidden. Can be set at any time, before or after the view loads. When it comes back (issue #13, as in the Facebook app): the bar hides only while the user drags down through content; it comes back at once, in every style, on background / foreground switches, a call, any system or in-app alert, a modal page, another key window, a push notification, a push or pop, and a memory warning, and hides again only on a new drag. Robust by design: a whitelist, not a list of events. The bar stays hidden only inside a hide session, started by the user scrolling down and bound to its context (page, tab, scroll view, window); anything else, also this controller's appear / disappear / size change and the keyboard, ends it and shows the bar. See docs/TabBar-Minimize-On-Scroll.md, "When the tab bar hides, and when it comes back". Same switch, Apple's API: on iOS 26+, `tabBarController.tabBarMinimizeBehavior = UITabBarMinimizeBehaviorOnScrollDown` does exactly the same in every style (CYLTabBarController overrides it; both read and write one value). Use this property where iOS 25 and earlier must be supported, since Apple's property does not exist there. | TODO |

| `CYLTabBarHostBadgeValue` | A view that shows only the tab bar of a CYLTabBarController made from a configuration (`+[CYLTabBarController tabBarControllerWithConfiguration:]`, see docs/Configuration-File.md). The pages belong to someone else: React Native, Flutter, or an app that draws its own content. Every tab gets a transparent, empty page. The React Native and Flutter components of `CrossPlatform/` are thin wrappers around it. - The tab bar controller is built once the view is in a window with a real width (a bar laid out at width 0 keeps its titles cut), and added as a child of the nearest view controller. - Image values given as URL strings (a file, or a dev server) are loaded on a background queue first, then the tab bar is built on the main queue; `imageResolver` handles other values (e.g. a Flutter asset). - Each view uses its own `CYLTabBarControllerContext` unless the configuration gives one, so several can be on screen. - Indexes (`selectedIndex`, `badgeValues`, `didSelectTab`) count the tabs of the configuration; the plus button is left out. CYLTabBarHostView *bar = [[CYLTabBarHostView alloc] init]; bar.didSelectTab = ^(NSInteger index, NSString *identifier) { [self showPageAtIndex:index]; }; bar.configuration = @{ CYLTabBarControllerTabBarItemsAttributes : items }; | TODO |

| `CYLTabBarPageRegistry` | A map from page IDs to page providers: a configuration (file, URL or dictionary) names each tab's page by a cross-platform string ID, and the app registers what that ID creates, so iOS and Android share one configuration. - `+sharedRegistry` is the global registry, used by every tab bar controller (like React Native's `AppRegistry`). - A registry you create is used by one tab bar controller only: pass it as `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry`. Several tab bars in one app can map the same ID to different pages. A tab's page is looked up in this order (`+defaultPageLookupOrder`; change it with `CYLTabBarControllerPageLookupOrder`); the first page found is used: 1. the registry passed as `CYLTabBarControllerPageRegistry` (any `CYLTabBarPageProviding`); 2. the resolver passed as `CYLTabBarControllerPageResolver`; 3. `+sharedRegistry`; 4. a view controller class that adopts `CYLTabBarPage` with that ID (registered automatically; turn it off with `CYLTabBarControllerAutomaticPageRegistration`); 5. none: the tab is skipped, listed in `-[CYLTabBarController cyl_skippedTabs]`, with a warning in DEBUG. The lookup itself is `+pagesOfTabs:registry:resolver:lookupOrder:keptTabs:skipped:`, which the tab bar controller calls; it can be called directly (e.g. by another container or in tests). Registration, lookup and creation happen on the main thread. | TODO |

(`-cyl_memoryWarningCellForTableView:`), row 2 switches the title offset of all tabs (`CYLTabBarController.titlePositionAdjustment`, issue #475), row 3 switches `tabBar.standardAppearance` themes, shared by Liquid Glass and FlatDesign, row 4 toggles the cached login state (`cyl_loggedIn`) and names the tabs that need login (issue #19), row 5 shows the plus button's touchable area and scales it with a slider (issue #91), row 6 selects the next tab by its index without the plus button (`cyl_selectedIndexIgnoringPlusButton`, issue #515), row 7 switches how the tab bar minimizes or hides on scroll (`cyl_tabBarMinimizeBehavior`, issue #13), row 8 switches the tap animation of the tabs, row 9 turns on the long press of the tabs, row 10 turns on swiping to switch tabs, row 11 shows a subview that responds outside its superview, row 12 loads an image from a bundle, row 13 hides the navigation bar without a base class, row 14 opens the slide transition demo, row 15 switches the tap sound and haptic, row 16 switches the long press duration and double tap interval, row 17 switches to the previous or next tab, row 18 runs the CYLUtils weak associated object and nearest control helpers (issue #535), row 19 pushes a tab bar controller whose plus button gets its image later (loaded, replaced, removed, or a background image), row 20 picks a skin (theme) of the tab bar (`CYLThemeManager`, `CYLTabBarTheme`, issue #216), row 21 lists the scroll hiding simulations in an action sheet (`-cyl_presentScrollHideSimulationMenu`, issue #13), row 22 creates a tab bar controller from a configuration file or URL (`UIViewController+CYLConfigurationDemo.h`), then the simulated failures of configurations, one row each (`-cyl_configurationEdgeCaseCellForTableView:row:`), then the in-place tab item updates (`-cyl_tabBarItemUpdateCellForTableView:row:`): title, icon, network icon, all network icons, all local icons,
